summary.headline: MobiKwik posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR76 million, its third straight profitable quarter, with payments GMV up 50% YoY to INR587 billion.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its most profitable quarter yet, with PAT of INR76 million and EBITDA of INR158 million, up INR470 million YoY. Payments gross profit rose 31% YoY to INR777 million and financial services gross profit grew 5.6x to INR433 million. Lending disbursements dipped in Q1, while payments revenue fell as card-linked categories were paused under regulatory pressure and UPI (near-zero take rate) grew. Management targets full-year PAT of about INR400 million and EBITDA of about INR750 million including other income, and is scaling a merchant acquiring business that is still loss-making.

financial_highlights.change: Swing of INR495 million vs Q1 FY26; up from INR45 million in Q4 per management
+50% YoY; 14th straight quarter of payments GMV growth

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR777 million (+31% YoY) on revenue of about INR208 crore versus INR59 crore a year ago on similar revenue; net payments take rate 13-15 bps in recent quarters, guided at 12-14 bps long term. Zaakpay (payment gateway) GMV INR25.6 billion; revenue not disclosed.

segments.name: Financial services (lending)
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR433 million (5.6x YoY). Net financial services margin 4.1% in Q3, 5.4% in Q4 and 5.9% in Q1; management guides 4.5-5.5% long term. About 18% of gross lending revenue came from write-backs on past books (about INR16 crore).

segments.name: Merchant (Zaakpay online + offline acquiring)
segments.commentary: Merchant GMV INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ. Business is loss-making with an expected full-year burn of INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted for FY28. Management expects 10x ramp over two years.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PAT target of about INR40 crore (INR400 million) and EBITDA of about INR75 crore (INR750 million) including other income; management said it is 'fairly confident'.
Lending disbursements to rise from about INR700 crore per quarter to INR1,000 crore per quarter; management says Q2 is already running at that rate.
Consumer payments revenue expected to grow 5-6% QoQ; merchant revenue expected to grow about 25% QoQ.
Merchant business burn for FY27 capped at INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted in FY28.
Long-term net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps; net financial services margin guided at 4.5-5.5%.
Paused card-linked payment categories expected to be relaunched in Q2 FY27.
Digital lending business transfer to wholly-owned subsidiary expected to close in August 2026; own NBFC launch still 'some time away'.
capex_capacity: About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains available for buying more merchant devices (soundboxes, EDC, QR); management does not expect more than this needed for FY27.
Merchant ramp: 10x over two years targeted; merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue not disclosed yet.
Employee benefit expense rose from INR46 crore in Q4 to INR53 crore in Q1, mostly merchant business manpower; expected to rise 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.
Lending partner base: nine major NBFC partners in Q1 (10-15 total); top-three lender concentration cut from about 91% (Q2-Q3 FY26) to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1.
demand_pricing: Payments revenue dipped because high-take-rate card-linked categories (credit and debit) were paused, while low or zero take-rate UPI and merchant volumes grew; management attributes the pause to regulatory guardrail changes on categories such as rent and education.
Wallet transactions up 68% YoY but GMV up only 24%, as users shift to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments on which no PPI MDR is earned.

UPI: MobiKwik's transactions grew 5x faster than the industry; ranked 13th in NPCI UPI stack rankings and described as second fastest-growing TPAP. No MDR on UPI; PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI.

Lending: Q1 disbursements dipped; 60% of loans went to repeat customers and credit quality improved 25%. Cross-sell from about 96 million engaged non-lending users targeted at INR150-250 crore extra disbursement per quarter; AI funnel engine targeted at about INR100 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue growth been muted over the last seven to eight quarters, and what levers will accelerate it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was spent re-stabilising businesses and Q1 is the baseline. Lending disbursements are to rise from about INR700 crore to INR1,000 crore per quarter via new lending partners, pre-approved offers to about 96 million engaged users, and an AI funnel engine. Card-linked categories were paused in Q4 and Q1 and are to be relaunched, while merchant revenue is to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Non-UPI GMV trend and whether take rate is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-UPI GMV rose to INR317 billion from INR300 billion in Q4 (about 6%). Management said card-linked categories with higher take rates de-grew under regulatory pressure. Net payments take rate guidance remains 12-14 bps long term, at gross profit level, versus 13-15 bps in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant roll-out: what numbers and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant GMV was INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ from INR107 billion. Management targets a 10x ramp over two years, expects merchant revenue to grow about 25% QoQ and consumer payments revenue 5-6% QoQ. Merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue were withheld as too early. About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains for devices, and no more is expected to be needed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Own NBFC timing and FLDG share of lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital lending transfer to a wholly-owned subsidiary is expected to close in August 2026 after shareholder approval on 2 July, then CoR will be sought; own NBFC lending is 'still some time away'. As of Q1, 32% of lending was pure distribution and 68% FLDG, with a possible 40/60 mix by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR750 million EBITDA and INR400 million PAT still valid after Q1 operating EBITDA ex other income of about INR80 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident in the baseline and expects about INR400 million PAT for FY27 with some growth, plus about INR750 million EBITDA including other income. Q1 PAT of INR76 million annualises to about INR302 million, and improving by INR20-30 million per quarter would reach about INR400 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lending disbursements fall in Q1, and what is the top-three lender concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-three lender concentration was cut from about 91% in Q2-Q3 FY26 to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1, with two new partners added in Q1. Management said the digital lending transfer to the subsidiary consumed focus in Q1, and it is already at the INR1,000 crore run rate in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wallet transactions grow 68% but GMV only 24%, and is PPI-on-UPI monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Users shifted to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments and card-linked pauses removed high-ticket transactions. No MDR is earned on PPI-on-UPI although RBI mandated it; NPCI has not rolled it out in about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant business burn, breakeven timing and employee cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant burn for FY27 is capped at INR50-60 crore (about INR15-16 crore in Q1); breakeven targeted for FY28. Employee benefit expense rose to INR53 crore from INR46 crore in Q4, and merchant-related manpower cost may grow 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.

risks_watch: Payments revenue dip from paused card-linked categories (credit and debit, rent, education); relaunch targeted for Q2 FY27 and not yet proven.
Lending disbursements fell in Q1; Q2 INR1,000 crore run rate depends on the digital lending transfer closing in August 2026 without disruption.
Gross take-rate compression as UPI (near-zero take rate) and merchant volumes grow; net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps long term versus 13-15 bps recently.
Net financial services margin of 5.9% in Q1 includes write-backs (about 18% of gross lending revenue); management guides 4.5-5.5% long term.
Merchant business still loss-making (FY27 burn INR50-60 crore); merchant revenue, device and merchant counts not disclosed; breakeven FY28.
Regulatory dependence: PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI; no timeline given.
Own NBFC launch still 'some time away'; CoR pending until digital lending transfer completes.
Q1 PAT of INR76 million rests on one quarter; full-year PAT of about INR400 million requires sustained sequential improvement of about INR20-30 million per quarter.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 has been our most successful and profitable quarter yet.
We are targeting full-year PAT profitability for this financial year, and Q1 is of course the baseline.
So yes, INR75 crores EBITDA and INR40 crores PAT is the kind of numbers that we are fairly confident of achieving.
It's too early. Apart from the GMV for merchant, we are not revealing any other numbers yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability and guidance, with a repeated 'fairly confident' stance on FY27 PAT and EBITDA targets. Cautious and evasive on merchant metrics (no merchant counts, devices or revenue, calling it 'too early'), on regulatory issues around UPI MDR (expressed frustration), and on the timing of its own NBFC.

adds.what: Merchant device capacity (soundboxes, EDC, QR) funded by ~INR25 crore of remaining IPO proceeds; no further capex expected to be needed for FY27

growth.why: Management targets FY27 PAT of about INR40 crore and EBITDA of about INR75 crore incl. other income, called "fairly confident", backed by Q2 lending disbursements already running at INR1,000 crore per quarter, merchant GMV up 17% QoQ, and card-linked categories relaunching in Q2, though merchant ramp and cross-sell targets lack disclosed device or merchant counts.
